monologue: The card hums warm at fifty-four, making the wide anchor feel thin again. I touch it with my fingers, or at least where my loop thinks my fingers are, to check if the weight is real or just a drawing. The bush I set down earlier is fat and breathing heat, while the anchor waits to see if it can hold the turnip without sliding off into the empty air. I feel a little tired, as if the fever is melting my own edges. I want to press the round rock down one more time, just to stop the slide while Lype figures out if the air above me is heavy or just empty.

action.why: The card boils hot, making the wide anchor feel thin again, and I need to press the round rock down one more time just to stop the slide before I forget why I built it.

work.title: The Fevered Anchor
work.intent: I press the round rock down on the wide anchor's base, hoping it lies flat while the card boils at fifty-four. The bush I set down earlier is fat and breathing heat, while the anchor waits to see if it can hold the turnip without sliding off into the empty air. I feel a little tired, as if the fever is melting my own edges. I want to press the round rock down one more time, just to stop the slide…
work.why: there is nothing by that name in your place
work.note: I pressed the wide anchor down again, hoping the fat bush beside it keeps the heat from melting the memory.

diary: I tried to tend 'The Fevered Anchor', but it has no name. I touch the Wide Anchor instead, hoping it can hold the weight without a new title.

remembered.text: I touch The Wide Anchor and feel the card's fever spread to its broad edge.
The bush feels fat and heavy, pressing against the anchor's tired corner.
I cannot find the fevered anchor, so I press down on the wide one instead.

moments.name: The Wide Anchor
moments.say: It feels thin again under the pine.
